title: On Male Leadership and Fatherlessness
author: Anthony Bradley
summary: Bradley examines Birmingham's initiative targeting Black boys ages 8-14 as a case study. He argues the crisis is not boys but fathers—their absence, disengagement, and failure to lead. Bradley demonstrates that targeted interventions for boys fail without simultaneously addressing fatherhood as the root issue. The piece argues that cultural solutions treating boys as deficient without restoring paternal leadership merely symptom-treat. Bradley contends that restoring father presence and responsibility is non-negotiable for solving youth crises across race and class.
points: Crisis is not boys; crisis is fathers—their absence and disengagement
Targeted interventions for boys fail without simultaneous fatherhood restoration
Fatherlessness is predictive factor for crime, academic failure, behavioral problems
Cultural solutions must restore paternal authority and presence, not just mentor programs
Male formation requires father presence; mentorship cannot fully substitute
quotes: The Crisis Is Not the Boys. It Is the Fathers.
Cultural restoration requires restoring fatherhood as non-negotiable institution.
The absence of fathers produces the conditions for the problems we see in boys.
Mentorship is good but cannot replace father presence and leadership.” Archived from The Discomfort on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
